title: About us
description: Meet the people, purpose and open technologies behind FOSSBot: an educational robot and browser-based platform developed through Harokopio University and GFOSS.

sections.title: Open robotics, built for learning
sections.text: FOSSBot brings together an educational robot and an open programming platform. Developed through collaboration between Harokopio University of Athens and GFOSS, it gives learners opportunities to build, program, experiment and understand the technology they use. Its software and robot designs are available for others to study, adapt and improve.

content.text: We want teachers and students to explore robotics through hands-on activities, creativity and experimentation. Affordable electronics, printable parts and open designs make it possible to repair the robot, extend its capabilities and adapt it to different learning activities.

FOSSBot grew from the 2019 Google Summer of Code project “A DIY robot kit for educators”, which produced the Proteas robot. The FOSSBot design was subsequently documented in a 2022 research publication by Christos Chronis and Iraklis Varlamis.
Today, the platform connects that work with browser-based Python and Blockly programming, a 3D simulator and physical robot control.

sections.title: From an idea to a working robot
sections.text: Learners can begin with visual blocks, develop their ideas in Python, and explore movement and sensors in a virtual environment or with a physical FOSSBot. The robot’s open design also makes building, repairing and adapting it part of the learning process.

content.text: FOSSBot has grown through contributions from students, researchers, developers and the open technologies community. The project repository credits Thanasis Apostolidis, Danai Brilli and Manousos Linardakis among its contributors.

The original research paper also acknowledges Dimitris Charitos, Giorgos Kazazis, George Yiannakoulias and GFOSS supporter Thodoros Karounos. These credits recognise contributions to the project’s development and history.
